column14: You can deploy OpenShift AI on Hosted Control Planes (HCP) running on OpenShift Virtualization.

column4: Support for IBM Power accelerated Triton Inference Server
column14: ⚠️2.x 문서에만 언급 — 3.x deprecated 여부 직접 확인 필요. You can deploy Triton inference server as a custom model serving runtime on IBM Power architecture as a Technology Preview feature in Red Hat OpenShift AI.

column4: Support for IBM Z accelerated Triton Inference Server
column14: ⚠️2.x 문서에만 언급 — 3.x deprecated 여부 직접 확인 필요. The Triton Inference Server can be deployed as a custom model serving runtime on IBM Z architecture as a Technology Preview feature in Red Hat OpenShift AI.

column4: Support for Intel Gaudi 3 accelerators
column14: ⚠️2.x 문서에만 언급 — 3.x deprecated 여부 직접 확인 필요. Support for Intel Gaudi 3 accelerators is now available.

column4: Support for Kubernetes Event-driven Autoscaling (KEDA)
column14: This Technology Preview feature enables metrics-based autoscaling for inference services, allowing for more efficient management of accelerator resources, reduced operational costs, and improved performance for your inference services.

column4: Support for Llama Stack and KubeRay on IBM Power
column14: Red Hat OpenShift AI 3.4 GA introduces official support for both Llama Stack and KubeRay on the IBM Power architecture.

column4: Support for Llama Stack Distribution version 0.2.22
column14: ⚠️2.x 문서에만 언급 — 3.x deprecated 여부 직접 확인 필요. The Llama Stack Distribution now includes Llama-stack version 0.2.22 as Technology Preview.

column4: Support for Llama Stack Distribution version 0.3.0
column14: The Llama Stack Distribution now includes version 0.3.0 as a Technology Preview feature.

column4: Support for multinode deployment of very large models
column14: Serving models over multiple graphical processing unit (GPU) nodes when using a single-model serving runtime is available as a Technology Preview feature.

column4: Support for NVIDIA NIM model serving platform
column14: ⚠️2.x 문서에만 언급 — 3.x deprecated 여부 직접 확인 필요. The NVIDIA NIM model serving platform adds support for deploying NVIDIA optimized models using NVIDIA NIM inference services in OpenShift AI.

column4: Support for OGX and KubeRay on IBM Power
column14: Red Hat OpenShift AI 3.5 EA1 introduces official support for both OGX (which replaces Llama Stack) and KubeRay on the IBM Power architecture.

column4: Support for OGX Distribution version 0.3.0
column14: The OGX Distribution includes version 0.3.0 as a Technology Preview feature.

column4: Support for text embedding models in the Model Catalog
column14: This Technology Preview feature allows data scientists and AI engineers to discover and deploy models designed specifically for vector generation, a critical component for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and semantic search workflows.

column4: Support for vLLM in IBM Power and IBM Z architectures
column14: ⚠️2.x 문서에만 언급 — 3.x deprecated 여부 직접 확인 필요. vLLM runtime templates are available for use in IBM Power and IBM Z architectures as Technology Preview.

column4: Targeted vLLM access-log filtering for LLMInferenceService
column14: The default LLMInferenceServiceConfig templates switch from the blanket --disable-uvicorn- access-log to vLLM 0.16’s --disable-access-log-for-endpoints /health,/metrics,/ping with a runtime fallback to the old flag on vLLM below 0.16.

column4: Task Shortcuts section added to the dashboard homepage
column14: The Red Hat OpenShift AI dashboard homepage includes a Task Shortcuts section.

column4: Telemetry collection for OGX API adoption metrics
column14: Telemetry data collection is introduced for OGX (formerly Llama Stack) API usage.

column4: Text-mode training for multimodal models in Training Hub
column14: Training Hub supports text-only training ("text mode") for multimodal model architectures.

column4: The Llama Stack Operator available on multi-architecture clusters
column14: The Llama Stack Operator is deployable on multi-architecture clusters in OpenShift AI version 3.3 and is available by default.

column4: The Llama Stack Operator with ConfigMap driven image updates
column14: The Llama Stack Operator in OpenShift AI 3.3 now offers ConfigMap driven image updates for LlamaStackDistribution resources.

column4: The Models-as-a-Service subscription model redesign
column14: The Models-as-a-Service (MaaS) subscription model has been redesigned to replace the tier-based model introduced in version 3.3.

column4: The OGX Operator available on multi-architecture clusters
column14: The OGX Operator is deployable on multi-architecture clusters in OpenShift AI version 3.3 and is available by default.

column4: The OGX Operator with ConfigMap driven image updates
column14: The OGX Operator in OpenShift AI 3.3 offers ConfigMap driven image updates for OGXServer resources.

column4: The remote::anthropic inference provider for OGX
column14: The remote::anthropic inference provider is available on OGX.

column4: The remote::gemini inference provider for OGX
column14: The remote::gemini inference provider is available on OGX.

column4: Thresholds support in evaluation runs in the OpenShift AI dashboard
column14: EvalHub introduces threshold configuration in evaluation runs as a Technology Preview.

column4: TLS and proxy configuration for all Llama Stack remote inference providers
column14: Red Hat OpenShift AI 3.4 EA2 introduces a standardized network configuration block for all Llama Stack remote inference providers.

column4: TLS and proxy configuration for all OGX remote inference providers
column14: Red Hat OpenShift AI 3.4 EA2 introduces a standardized network configuration block for all OGX remote inference providers.

column4: Tool calling metadata on model cards in the model catalog
column14: Red Hat OpenShift AI now displays tool callin, also known as function calling, configuration metadata directly in the model catalog.

column4: Trace archival support for MLflow at scale
column14: You can use age-based trace archival for MLflow to manage large volumes of trace data.

column4: Training Hub RLVR and GRPO dependencies in universal workbench images
column14: The universal workbench image includes all dependencies required for Reinforcement Learning from Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) and Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) training workflows.

column4: Training images and ClusterTrainingRuntimes for Kubeflow Training Operator v1
column14: The Kubeflow Training Operator (v1) is deprecated starting OpenShift AI 2.25 and is scheduled to be removed.

column4: TrustyAI–Llama Stack integration for safety, guardrails, and evaluation
column14: You can now use the Guardrails Orchestrator from TrustyAI with Llama Stack as a Technology Preview feature.

column4: TrustyAI–OGX integration for safety, guardrails, and evaluation
column14: You can use the Guardrails Orchestrator from TrustyAI with OGX as a Technology Preview feature.

column4: Unified dashboard experience for generative AI model deployment workflows
column14: Generative AI model deployment workflows are in a unified dashboard experience, replacing separate entry points for different model serving runtimes with a single guided wizard.

column4: Unified MaaS governance page for subscriptions and authorization policies
column14: This enhancement combines the Subscriptions and Authorization policies pages in Settings into a single MaaS governance page, accessible from Settings → MaaS governance.

column4: Updated naming of resources to include data-science prefix
column14: To ensure a consistent naming convention across the product, resource naming is now updated to include the data-science- prefix.

column4: Updated workbench images
column14: ⚠️2.x 문서에만 언급 — 3.x deprecated 여부 직접 확인 필요. A new set of workbench images is now available.

column4: Upgrade vLLM Gaudi SW 1.22.2 + vLLM v0.9.0.1 in RHOAI_2.25.1
column14: ⚠️2.x 문서에만 언급 — 3.x deprecated 여부 직접 확인 필요. Support for vLLM Inference Server with Intel Gaudi 1.21 accelerators is now available in Red Hat OpenShift AI 2.25.1.

column4: Upgrading vLLM Gaudi to 1.20 release
column14: ⚠️2.x 문서에만 언급 — 3.x deprecated 여부 직접 확인 필요. vLLM now supports version 1.20 of the Intel Gaudi Operator.

column4: Use an existing Argo Workflows instance with pipelines
column14: ⚠️2.x 문서에만 언급 — 3.x deprecated 여부 직접 확인 필요. You can now configure OpenShift AI to use an existing Argo Workflows instance instead of the one included with Data Science Pipelines.

column4: Use Guardrails Orchestrator with LlamaStack
column14: ⚠️2.x 문서에만 언급 — 3.x deprecated 여부 직접 확인 필요. You can now run detections using the Guardrails Orchestrator tool from TrustyAI with Llama Stack as a Technology Preview feature, using the built-in detection component.

column4: User-request header routing for external OGX providers
column14: You can pass specific user-request headers to external OGX (formerly Llama Stack) providers.

column4: Validated sdg-hub notebooks for Red Hat AI Platform
column14: Validated sdg_hub example notebooks are available to provide a notebook-driven user experience in OpenShift AI 3.0.

column4: Validated tool-calling configuration for models in the model catalog
column14: The model catalog displays validated vLLM deployment arguments for models with confirmed tool- calling support.

column4: Verify connection credentials before saving
column14: This feature is available as a Technology Preview.

column4: View external model endpoints in the dashboard
column14: You can view registered external model endpoints and their associated provider details from the → OpenShift AI dashboard.

column4: View running agent deployments in the dashboard
column14: In OpenShift AI, you can view a list of running agent deployments directly in the dashboard.

column4: View the vLLM version for distributed inference deployments
column14: When using distributed inference with Distributed Inference with llm-d, platform administrators can Red Hat OpenShift AI Self-Managed 3.5 Release notes view the version of vLLM that is running directly from the OpenShift AI dashboard.

column4: vLLM runtime support for Models-as-a-Service
column14: This Technology Preview feature enables you to serve large language models with vLLM’s high- performance inference capabilities while benefiting from MaaS governance and subscription-based controls.

column4: vLLM uvicorn access logs are disabled by default in Distributed Inference with llm-d
column14: vLLM uvicorn access logs are disabled by default in LLMInferenceServiceConfig, including logs generated by router-scheduler /metrics endpoint polling.

column4: vLLM-Gaudi 1.23 support
column14: Red Hat OpenShift AI 3.3 now supports vllm-gaudi version 1.23, enhancing, enhancing performance and stability of vLLM applications.

column4: Workbench and runtime images default to Red Hat Python index
column14: Workbench and runtime images default to the Red Hat Python index.

column4: Workbench and runtime images default to the Red Hat Python index
column14: Access and use Red Hat built and supported Python packages.

column4: Workload variant autoscaler for Distributed Inference with llm-d model deployments
column14: Platform Operators can enable autoscaling for Distributed Inference with llm-d model deployments based on incoming request volume as a Technology Preview.
